comments.body:
Reproduced deterministically: a `git` wrapper that execs `sleep` for the target subcommand, with `_GIT_TIMEOUT` set to 1 s. Against a repo with `origin` configured and a valid HEAD, `has_remote` returned False for a slow `git remote`, and `resolve_ref("HEAD", fetch=False)` raised SnapshotRefError "cannot resolve ref 'HEAD'" for a slow `git rev-parse`.

Root cause: `git_run` folded TimeoutExpired into a private rc-124 result, and `rev_parse`/`has_remote` read its empty stdout as "no SHA" / "no remotes".

Fix (Gerrit 3258): `git_run` -> `gitutil.run_git_bounded`; `has_remote` and `rev_parse` check `git_outcome.is_watchdog_timeout` and raise SnapshotError naming the operation and bound (not SnapshotRefError, so the attested materializer's `except SnapshotRefError` fallback does not swallow it). `_ensure_blobs_present` still skips silently on that error, keeping its best-effort contract. Tests: tests/unit/test_snapshot_git_watchdog_d33f.py (6; 4 failed before the fix). Lint and typecheck pass; 967 snapshot/delta-tree/workflow tests and 3083 tests referencing the snapshot module pass.

compiled_state.description:
## Observation

`rebar._snapshot.git_fetch.git_run` folds a `TimeoutExpired` (300 s `_GIT_TIMEOUT`) into a private synthetic `CompletedProcess(rc=124, "git timed out after 300s")`. Its callers read that result as a semantic answer:

- `rev_parse` returns `None` on any failure, so a timed-out `git rev-parse` makes `repo_snapshot.resolve_ref` raise `SnapshotRefError("cannot resolve ref … Name a valid branch, tag, or full SHA …")` — a wrong-input verdict for a slow or wedged git call.
- `has_remote` parses `git remote` stdout; a timeout yields empty stdout, so it answers "no such remote" and `resolve_ref` / `_ensure_blobs_present` skip the fetch path.
- `is_present_full_sha` answers False (safe: it falls through to a fetch).

Found by code reading while auditing private rc-124 folds for `unarmed-raw-siskin`. Not reproduced.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `git_run` uses `gitutil.run_git_bounded` instead of its private fold.
- [ ] A timed-out `rev-parse` in `resolve_ref` is reported as a timeout naming the operation and bound, not as an unresolvable ref.
- [ ] A timed-out `git remote` in `has_remote` is not read as "remote absent".
- [ ] Regression tests drive each timeout and assert the report.
compiled_state.title: git_fetch.git_run reads a timed-out rev-parse/remote as 'cannot resolve ref' / 'no remote'
